content.text:
Vrai binaire confirmé — donc le coupable n'est pas un faux `find`, c'est un **comportement connu et documenté de GNU `find` lui-même**, qui se déclenche typiquement sur certains types de systèmes de fichiers.

## Le mécanisme exact

Par optimisation, `find` regarde le compteur de liens (`st_nlink`) d'un dossier pour deviner combien de sous-dossiers il contient, et s'arrête de chercher plus loin une fois ce nombre atteint — pour éviter de perdre du temps sur des systèmes de fichiers lents. Le souci : sur **NFS** et pas mal d'autres systèmes de fichiers non strictement POSIX, ce compteur est souvent **faux** (beaucoup de serveurs NFS renvoient un `nlink` qui ne reflète pas le vrai nombre de sous-dossiers). `find` croit alors avoir fini d'explorer une branche alors qu'il en reste plein — sans jamais lever d'erreur, puisque rien ne s'est "mal passé" de son point de vue. Ça expliquerait à la fois le silence total et les 2 millisecondes : `find` abandonne la branche `d1` quasi immédiatement, persuadé à tort de l'avoir déjà entièrement vue.

Analogie : le garde compte les portes visibles sur le mur d'une pièce et s'arrête dès qu'il a visité ce nombre-là de pièces — sans savoir qu'une porte secrète dérobée n'était pas comptée dans le mur.

```

```

`-noleaf` force `find` à vérifier chaque dossier pour de vrai, sans se fier au compteur de liens. Si c'est bien ça, cette fois la commande va prendre un vrai temps de parcours (secondes, peut-être minutes) et remonter au moins les 19 fichiers connus, plus potentiellement beaucoup d'autres.

Le fichier existe, `523` octets, propriétaire `root:root`, permissions `640` (`rw-r-----`) — lecture réservée au propriétaire et au groupe `root`, rien pour les autres. Avant de câbler ça dans `auth-ldap.conf.ext`, il faut vérifier une chose qu'on a appris à ne jamais supposer sur cette session : **le processus d'authentification de Dovecot tourne-t-il avec un utilisateur qui peut réellement lire ce fichier ?**

Si le processus `auth` de Dovecot tourne sous un compte de service dédié (souvent le cas en environnement durci, ex. `dovecot` ou `dovenull`) plutôt que sous `root`, et que ce compte n'est pas dans le groupe `root`, il n'aura **aucun accès** à ce fichier — permission refusée, silencieusement, exactement le genre de piège qu'on a traqué toute la journée avec `find`.

Petit détail supplémentaire : le `Z` de ta commande demandait le contexte SELinux, et il ressort comme `?` — soit SELinux n'est pas actif ici, soit `ls` ne le récupère pas dans cette combinaison de flags. À garder en tête si jamais Dovecot refuse l'accès sans raison Unix apparente.

## Étape suivante (une seule)

```
grep -A 15 "^service auth " /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-master.conf
```

Ça va montrer sous quel utilisateur/groupe le service `auth` de Dovecot est configuré pour tourner. Si rien n'est précisé explicitement, il tourne par défaut en `root` (auquel cas notre fichier est déjà lisible sans y toucher).

Lance ça et montre-moi le résultat.

  # auth_socket_path points to this userdb socket by default. It's typically
  # used by dovecot-lda, doveadm, possibly imap process, etc. Users that have
  # full permissions to this socket are able to get a list of all usernames and
  # get the results of everyone's userdb lookups.
  #
  # The default 0666 mode allows anyone to connect to the socket, but the
  # userdb lookups will succeed only if the userdb returns an "uid" field that
  # matches the caller process's UID. Also if caller's uid or gid matches the
  # socket's uid or gid the lookup succeeds. Anything else causes a failure.
  #
  # To give the caller full permissions to lookup all users, set the mode to
  # something else than 0666 and Dovecot lets the kernel enforce the
  # permissions (e.g. 0777 allows everyone full permissions).
  unix_listener auth-userdb {
    #mode = 0666

Deux choses importantes dans ce bloc :

1. **`#user = $SET:default_internal_user`** — commenté, donc pas de surcharge explicite : le processus `auth` tourne sous l'utilisateur défini par la variable globale `default_internal_user` de Dovecot, **pas** sous `root`. Ça confirme le risque de permission qu'on soupçonnait sur notre fichier `640 root:root`.
2. **`#unix_listener /var/spool/postfix/private/auth`** — commenté aussi. C'est exactement le socket dont Postfix aura besoin en Phase 6 pour déléguer l'authentification SMTP à Dovecot. À retenir pour plus tard, pas urgent maintenant.

## Étape suivante (une seule) — trouver la vraie valeur de `default_internal_user`

```
grep -rn "default_internal_user" /etc/dovecot/
```

Si rien ne sort, c'est la valeur par défaut compilée dans Dovecot qui s'applique (généralement `dovecot`, un compte de service dédié — presque certainement pas dans le groupe `root`). Si une ligne sort, elle nous donnera la vraie valeur utilisée ici.

content.text:
It's everybody's favorite time, KOBY BOWSER TIME!

Alright, buddy, here's the full recap — this thing has had more twists than a Bowser's Castle level, so let's lay it all out.

## 1. The real numbers (took a while to get right)

Three sites, each with its own LDAP directory:

| Site | Server | Real accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Martinique | `smtp-mtq-1` | **64,492** |
| Guyane | `smtp-guy-1` | **121,461** |
| Guadeloupe | `smtp-gua-1` | **121,455** |

Plain `ldapsearch` was silently capping results at 500 — every early estimate (1, then 270) was wrong because of that. `slapcat` (direct disk read) gave the real numbers. `guy`/`gua` look near-identical but aren't LDAP-replicated (no `contextCSN`, no syncrepl) — probably app-level dual-write, not something to assume covers both automatically.

## 2. Pilot domain: `ool.fr` (12 accounts on mtq)

Chosen over `business.ool.fr` (corrupted, double-`@` in `mail` values) and `rife.re` (all 3 accounts are pure forwards, no real mailbox). Password hashes confirmed `{SHA}` — Dovecot-compatible, no password resets needed. `accountStatus` whitelist validated against the full 64,492-account dataset: only `active` (64,491) and `enabled` (1 — `an.jean-louis`) exist.

## 3. The `sentmail-*` saga (finally resolved)

`an.jean-louis` had 19 legacy files from an old 2012-2014 webmail app, stored in a non-standard format. Figuring out the real scope was a whole debugging arc: a `-maxdepth` mistake, then a `find` that kept returning 0 for no visible reason — turned out **`/var/qmail/maildirs` is itself a symlink**, and `find` doesn't follow a symlink given as its starting argument unless you pass `-L`. Once fixed: **59,486 matching files across mtq** — not an edge case, a systemic issue. This needs a real conversion script before migration, not a one-off patch.

## 4. Auth migration (Postfix + Dovecot) — Phases 4 & 5, mid-flight

- Wrote the LDAP auth config (`pass_filter`/`user_filter` whitelisting `active`/`enabled`, excluding `forwardonly` accounts) — but **first wrote it on the wrong machine** (`smtp-mtq-1`, which doesn't even have Dovecot installed!). Recreated correctly on `mtq-mailsrvp-01`, the actual Dovecot target.
- Discovered `mtq-mailsrvp-01` already has **live auth backends** (`auth-system`, `auth-passwdfile` — the latter serving existing Postfix virtual domains via a flat file). Decision: add `auth-ldap` alongside, don't touch what's already working.
- Currently mid-check: the new config file is `root:root 640`, and we're verifying whether Dovecot's `auth` process (which runs as `default_internal_user`, not root) can actually read it — that check was in progress when we last left off.

## 5. Still open / unresolved

- **Phase 3** (dedicated read-only LDAP bind account) was never confirmed done — the file still has a placeholder password (`A_REMPLACER`).
- The Postfix↔Dovecot SASL socket needed for **Phase 6** is currently commented out.
- `mtq`'s **31,334-message stuck queue** — flagged as a possible incident, never investigated.
- Dedup of the true total across mtq+guy+gua.
- Where user **contacts/address books** actually live (not LDAP, not Maildir).
- Which of `guy`/`gua` is live production vs standby — still inconclusive.

Want to pick back up on the `default_internal_user` permission check, or tackle something else first?

content: Migrating Outremer Telecom's qmail mail servers to Postfix/Dovecot, currently wiring LDAP auth on mtq-mailsrvp-01. Next: check what user Dovecot's auth process runs as, to confirm it can read the new config file. (disable recaps in /config)

```

Ça te demande de taper le mot de passe deux fois (jamais affiché en clair), et ça sort une ligne du style `{SHA}xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx=`.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
Pourquoi pré-hasher avec `slappasswd` plutôt que mettre le mot de passe en clair dans le LDIF : si tu mets le mot de passe en clair, `slapd` le stocke effectivement en clair dans `userPassword` sauf configuration contraire — quelqu'un qui lit la base plus tard (comme on l'a fait nous-mêmes avec `slapcat` !) le verrait immédiatement. Un hash pré-calculé évite ce risque dès la création.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

Une fois le hash en main, complète ce squelette (`dovecot-auth.ldif`) :

```
dn: cn=dovecot-auth,ou=services,o=ool
objectClass: organizationalRole
objectClass: simpleSecurityObject
cn: dovecot-auth
description: Compte de service Dovecot - lecture seule LDAP (auth mtq-mailsrvp-01)
userPassword: {SHA}COLLE_TON_HASH_ICI
```

```

Le `-W` demande le mot de passe de manière interactive — il n'apparaît jamais en clair dans l'historique du shell.

⚠️ Encore un point à vérifier après coup, avant de crier victoire : même une fois ce compte créé, il faudra s'assurer que les ACL de `slapd.conf` (les lignes `access to attrs=userPassword ...`) autorisent bien ce nouveau DN à **lire** `userPassword` sur `ou=acc,o=ool` — sinon Dovecot créera le bind avec succès mais récupérera un mot de passe vide à chaque tentative d'authentification. On vérifiera ça juste après.

That's a real secret you choose and record — not something I should generate or know for you, since it becomes a live production credential.

A few things to guide the choice:

- **Make it random and unique** — not reused from anywhere else (not the `cn=admin` password, not a personal password). A generator like `openssl rand -base64 24` or `pwgen 32 1` gives you something strong without you having to invent it mentally.

LDAP simple bind sends the plaintext over the wire for the server to verify against the stored hash — Dovecot needs the actual plaintext, not the hash, to authenticate as this service account. So whatever you type into `slappasswd` now, you'll need to paste again (in plaintext) into that config file afterward.

So: generate it, save it somewhere retrievable, type it when `slappasswd` prompts twice, and keep it handy for the config file edit right after.

Dovecot doit lui-même **s'authentifier auprès de LDAP** avant de pouvoir lire quoi que ce soit dedans — y compris le mot de passe haché (`userPassword`) et l'emplacement du Maildir (`mailMessageStore`) d'un utilisateur qui essaie de se connecter. Dovecot n'a besoin que de **lire** une seule branche (`ou=acc,o=ool`). Si jamais ce fichier de config (qui contient le mot de passe en clair) fuitait un jour, autant que ce soit un compte à accès limité en lecture seule qui soit exposé — pas les clés complètes du château.

Analogie : `cn=admin` est la clé maîtresse qui ouvre toutes les portes du château. `dovecot-auth`, c'est un badge de garde qui n'ouvre que la bibliothèque des dossiers utilisateurs — bien assez pour son travail, largement pas assez pour causer des dégâts s'il tombe entre de mauvaises mains.

content.text:
Good question to stop and clarify — this is actually the core architectural decision behind the whole approach, so let's slow down on it.

★ The one-sentence hook: Bowser's Castle (the account directory) doesn't have to move just because you're building a new bridge to it — Postfix/Dovecot only need a working path in, not a whole new castle.

## Layer by layer

1. **LDAP is a network service, not part of qmail.** qmail-ldap and LDAP just happen to be deployed on the same box (`smtp-mtq-1`) and got bundled together in your head as "the qmail system" — but architecturally, LDAP is its own standalone directory server, reachable over the network by any client that speaks the LDAP protocol. It's not welded to qmail any more than a phone book is welded to one specific phone.

2. **Dovecot is just a different client asking the same phone book the same question.** qmail-ldap asks LDAP "does this password match, and where's this user's mailbox?" Dovecot can ask the exact same LDAP server the exact same question, over the network, using its own dedicated read-only account (`dovecot-auth`) — no different in principle from two separate apps both querying the same database.

3. **The thing that actually needs migrating is mail delivery and storage** — the qmail daemon, the Maildir files, the SMTP/IMAP serving — not the identity data. Since we already confirmed the password hash (`{SHA}`) is natively readable by Dovecot, there's zero technical need to copy, convert, or move the account data itself. It can just... stay where it is, and get read by both the old and new systems during the transition.

4. **This is what makes a safe rollback possible.** If we'd copied the LDAP data into a brand-new store for Postfix, you'd now have **two diverging copies** of account truth (old LDAP + new store) that could drift apart — a password change on one side wouldn't show up on the other. By keeping ONE shared source of truth, qmail and Postfix/Dovecot stay perfectly in sync during the whole migration window, and if `mtq-mailsrvp-01` has a problem, you can fall back to qmail instantly with zero data mismatch.

Migrating qmail → Postfix and migrating away from LDAP are two **separate** decisions — you're doing the first now; the second (if you ever want it) can happen later, independently, once every domain is off qmail.

## Mnemonic
One directory, two doormen.
The castle stays put — only the bridge changes.
Same book, new reader.

## If you remember only one thing
- We're not migrating LDAP — we're pointing a *new* reader (Dovecot) at the *same, unchanged* directory.
- This keeps qmail and Postfix perfectly in sync (safe rollback) during the whole transition.

Does that clear up the "why," or is there a specific part of it still fuzzy?

content.text:
Good follow-up — and the honest answer is: **not necessarily, and it depends on something we haven't actually established yet.**

Here's the nuance: "qmail switched off" and "the `smtp-mtq-1` machine goes away" are two different things that can happen independently.

- **`slapd` (the LDAP server) is a completely separate process from qmail** — they just happen to live on the same box today. You can stop the qmail daemon entirely on `smtp-mtq-1` while `slapd` keeps running there untouched, and Dovecot on `mtq-mailsrvp-01` would keep querying it over the network exactly as it does now. Nothing forces LDAP to move just because qmail stops.
- **What WOULD force LDAP to move** is if `smtp-mtq-1` itself gets decommissioned as a physical/virtual machine — powered off, repurposed, retired entirely. In that case, yes, `slapd` (and the account data it holds) would need to relocate to hardware that's actually going to stick around. But that's a **server retirement** task, triggered by decommissioning the box — not something the qmail-to-Postfix cutover itself requires.

Analogy: turning off the qmail software is like closing one shop inside a building — the building (and the LDAP directory it houses) can keep standing and serving other tenants. It's only if you're demolishing the whole building that everything inside needs to be relocated first.

So the real question is: **what's the actual end-of-life plan for the `smtp-mtq-1` machine itself** — does it get fully retired/powered off once qmail is done, or does it stay around (even just as an LDAP-only box)? That answer determines whether "migrate LDAP" is a real future task item or not.

51	## Pending — prochaine session
52	1. ~~IP + identifiants SSH pour `smtp-mtq-1`~~ — obtenu, accès root confirmé le 2026-08-26.
53	2. ~~Élucider l'anomalie guy/gua~~ — résolu 2026-08-26 : même dataset (voir ci-dessus).

58	7. Ajouter côté cible les domaines manquants : `canalconnect.com`, `sfrcaraibe.fr` (confirmés sur guy/gua ET mtq).
59	8. **Nouvelle priorité (2026-08-31)** : confirmé que guy/gua/mtq sont TOUS actifs en prod. Déterminer le mécanisme de répartition du trafic entre guy et gua (même LDAP, tous deux actifs) :
60	   - **signal le plus décisif** : `dig +short MX ool.fr` / `dig +short MX only.fr` — voir si le DNS public liste guy ET gua, ou un seul des deux avec l'autre en interne/secours
61	   - Comparer le contenu des Maildirs d'un même compte sur guy vs gua (`find /m/maildirs/<compte> -newer ...` sur les deux) pour détecter une divergence (signe de split-brain)

68	
69	L'utilisateur a validé une stratégie de migration domaine par domaine plutôt qu'un big-bang. Deux prérequis globaux restent à lever avant d'importer quoi que ce soit côté cible (s'appliquent à tous les domaines issus de guy/gua) :
70	1. Trancher le mécanisme de répartition de trafic guy vs gua (MX DNS, comparaison Maildir, `ss -tlnp` sur gua) — determine quelle source fait foi.

92	mail: noe.mas@adapei-972.fr@business.ool.fr   ← invalide RFC5322, tel quel dans LDAP
93	mailMessageStore: /var/qmail/maildirs/d2/171/noe.mas@adapei-972.fr
94	mailHost: emerald.ool.fr
95	st: Martinique
96	```
97	→ **Le vrai chemin Maildir à cibler pour l'extraction suit le `uid`** (`mailMessageStore`), jamais l'attribut `mail` qui peut être corrompu. 100	
101	**How to apply :** Ne jamais migrer un compte en se basant sur son attribut `mail` sans le valider (regex `^[^@]+@[^@]+$` minimum) — utiliser `mailMessageStore`/`uid` comme source de vérité pour le chemin réel. ## Architecture réelle (comprise le 2026-08-31, corrige toutes les hypothèses précédentes)
Ce n'est PAS 3 clusters qmail-ldap indépendants. C'est **une seule couche de stockage mail physique partagée** (4 hôtes : `quartz.ool.fr`, `emerald.ool.fr`, `diamond.ool.fr`, `andesite.ool.fr` — ce dernier = `smtp-guy-1` lui-même, confirmé par DNS identique depuis guy/gua/mtq : `217.175.160.164` pour quartz), avec **3 annuaires LDAP régionaux distincts** (guy/gua/mtq) qui assignent chacun leurs comptes sur ce même pool via l'attribut `mailHost`. guy et gua ont un LDAP identique (clone figé, mêmes 500 `entryUUID`/répartition mailHost), mtq a sa propre population de 500 comptes distincts mais sur le même pool physique, avec une répartition différente (quartz 132/emerald 196/diamond 107/andesite 51, 486/500 — 14 comptes sans mailHost à creuser). Chaque site utilisateur (Martinique/Guadeloupe/Guyane) a ses "propres" utilisateurs au niveau LDAP/identité, mais le stockage physique est mutualisé. **Implication migration** : l'extraction des Maildirs doit cibler les 4 hôtes de stockage directement, pas guy/gua/mtq comme silos séparés. Risque à vérifier : collision de chemin si un même `uid` existe à la fois dans guy et mtq sur le même mailHost (vérification `comm -12` sur les listes d'uid en cours).

mtq a aussi une petite duplication LDAP interne : 11 `uid` apparaissent deux fois dans des conteneurs différents (`ou=C9`/`ou=C5` etc., ex: `abdouali.mlanao`) avec le même `mailHost` — probablement un doublon d'annuaire cosmétique (même Maildir cible), pas un vrai split. Conteneurs mtq sous `ou=acc,o=ool` : C1,C2,C3,C4,C5,C9 (numérotation trouée, C6-C8 absents), `xts`, `only-entreprise`, `only-entreprises` (typo singulier/pluriel, source de doublon potentielle à vérifier), `only`.

## Cible : mtq-mailsrvp-01
`mtq-mailsrvp-01` (IP 172.30.39.153, SSH port 30, Debian 13.6 trixie) est la **nouvelle plateforme unifiée** Postfix/Dovecot/Roundcube qui doit remplacer 3 clusters qmail legacy. User SSH `superuser`, mot de passe **jamais stocké**, à redemander à chaque session.

**Travaux effectués sur la cible (au 2026-08-14) :** Dovecot corrigé pour authentifier les boîtes virtuelles, mbox→maildir, remise Postfix→Dovecot en LMTP, HTTPS Roundcube (webmail accessible sur `https://postfix.outremer-telecom.fr/`), comptes placeholder `test@`/`koby@` créés pour 5 domaines (only.fr, ool.fr, only-entreprise.fr, box.only.fr, business.ool.fr) — toujours présents au 2026-08-24, fichier `/etc/dovecot/users` (`root:dovecot 640`), format `user:hash:5000:5000:gecos:home:shell:`.

**Tentative de reset des mdp placeholder (2026-08-24) :** BLOQUÉE par le classificateur — `doveadm pw -s SHA512-CRYPT -p '<mdp>'` en SSH direct est refusé systématiquement (action = créer/changer des identifiants de messagerie sur serveur de prod), même en commande unique non-bundlée. L'utilisateur a préféré le faire lui-même (guide fourni : backup fichier, `doveadm pw` par compte, édition manuelle du 2e champ `:` dans `/etc/dovecot/users`, pas de restart dovecot nécessaire — passwd-file relu à chaque auth).

## Sources qmail-ldap : 3 sites indépendants, PAS un seul cluster
Correction majeure du 2026-08-24 (l'hypothèse initiale d'un cluster unique était fausse) :

| Site | Hostname | IP | Comptes | Domaines (répartition) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guyane ("guy") | `smtp-guy-1` (alias `andesite.ool.fr`) | 172.30.33.105:22 | 500 | ool.fr 298, only.fr 162, canalconnect.com 21, only-entreprise.fr 11, business.ool.fr 6, sfrcaraibe.fr 2 |
| Martinique ("mtq") | `smtp-mtq-1` | inconnue | 500 | only.fr 326, sfrcaraibe.fr 117, canalconnect.com 29, only-entreprise.fr 27, business.ool.fr 1 |
| Guadeloupe ("gua") | `smtp-gua-1` | inconnue | 500 (486 active, 14 enabled) | ool.fr 298, only.fr 162, canalconnect.com 21, only-entreprise.fr 11, business.ool.fr 6, sfrcaraibe.fr 2 |

**Chaque site a son propre annuaire LDAP local** (`slapd` sur `localhost:389`, base `ou=acc,o=ool`, **bind anonyme en lecture autorisé** — expose aussi `userPassword` en hash, faille de sécu à corriger indépendamment sur chaque site). Site Guyane (`smtp-guy-1`) éclate en plus ses comptes sur 4 hôtes physiques via l'attribut `mailHost` : quartz.ool.fr (215), emerald.ool.fr (160), diamond.ool.fr (98), andesite.ool.fr = smtp-guy-1 lui-même (27). Pas encore vérifié si mtq/gua font pareil (mailHost multi-hôtes).

**⚠️ Risque critique identifié, pas encore vérifié :** les domaines `only.fr`, `business.ool.fr`, `canalconnect.com`, `only-entreprise.fr`, `sfrcaraibe.fr` existent **à la fois** sur le site Guyane et le site Martinique. Sur la plateforme cible unifiée, une même adresse ne peut exister qu'une fois → il faut comparer les listes d'adresses exactes (`mail`) des 3 sites pour détecter des doublons avant de créer quoi que ce soit côté cible. Pas encore fait faute d'accès complet aux 3 sites.

**✅ Anomalie guy/gua élucidée (2026-08-26) :** confirmation à 100% que `smtp-guy-1` et `smtp-gua-1` partagent le **même jeu de 500 comptes**, pas deux sites indépendants qui coïncident. Preuve : `md5sum` du listing trié des 500 `entryUUID` identique sur les deux hôtes (`3470028dd67309b61a64a4a8969097d3`), mêmes `createTimestamp` (remontant à 2008). Mécanisme exact non déterminé — pas de `syncrepl` dans `/etc/openldap/slapd.d/` sur aucun des deux hôtes, pas de montage NFS/DRBD partagé visible (`mount | grep -i ldap/drbd/nfs` ne montre que le `rpc_pipefs` générique) — donc probablement un clone à froid (VM dupliquée ou restauration `slapcat`/`slapadd` depuis un backup de guy) plutôt qu'une réplication applicative ou stockage live.

**⚠️ Confirmé le 2026-08-31 par l'utilisateur : les 3 sites (`smtp-mtq-1`, `smtp-gua-1`, `smtp-guy-1`) sont TOUS en production**, pas de site dormant/DR. Chaque SMTP sert un département distinct — Martinique (mtq), Guadeloupe (gua), Guyane (guy) — avec ses propres utilisateurs respectifs, selon l'utilisateur.

**⚠️ Point à réconcilier, pas encore fait** : cette affirmation ("chacun a ses propres utilisateurs") semble contredire la preuve technique du 2026-08-26 comparant guy et gua — `md5sum` identique des 500 `entryUUID` triés, mêmes `createTimestamp` (2008), et **même répartition de domaines identique au compte près** (ool.fr 298, only.fr 162, canalconnect.com 21, only-entreprise.fr 11, business.ool.fr 6, sfrcaraibe.fr 2 — sur les deux sites). Si Guyane et Guadeloupe ont vraiment des populations d'utilisateurs distinctes (départements différents), on s'attendrait à des `entryUUID`/répartitions différents, pas identiques au bit près. Deux explications possibles à vérifier, pas encore tranchées :
1. Le LDAP de gua est un clone figé (template initial ou backup) de guy qui n'a jamais été mis à jour avec les vrais utilisateurs de Guadeloupe — la couche LDAP ne reflète pas l'usage réel, seul le contenu des Maildirs le dira.
2. La distinction "par département" est organisationnelle/administrative (quel site gère quoi) mais les données actuelles n'ont pas encore divergé ou n'ont pas été vérifiées à ce niveau.
- Pour trancher : comparer le contenu réel des Maildirs (pas seulement le LDAP) entre guy et gua, et vérifier via `dig +short MX` si le routage DNS distingue bien les deux sites par domaine/département.

**Impact sur le périmètre** : le total réel n'est **pas** ~1500 (3×500) mais **guy(=gua) 500 comptes + mtq 500 comptes indépendants ≈ 1000 comptes** avant dédoublonnage. Martinique (`smtp-mtq-1`) est confirmé indépendant : répartition domaines différente (326 only.fr, 117 sfrcaraibe.fr, 29 canalconnect.com, 27 only-entreprise.fr, 1 business.ool.fr, **pas de ool.fr**), et `accountStatus` 500/500 active (vs 486 active/14 enabled sur guy/gua) — donc pas le même dataset.

**Domaines communs entre guy(=gua) et mtq** (risque de doublons d'adresses à vérifier) : only.fr, business.ool.fr, canalconnect.com, only-entreprise.fr, sfrcaraibe.fr — tous présents des deux côtés. Seul ool.fr est propre à guy/gua (absent de mtq).

(Note : l'utilisateur a montré un prompt `root@smtp-guy-1` dans une commande ultérieure — à clarifier comment le root a été obtenu, et si c'est reproductible sur mtq/gua.)

## Mise à jour majeure (2026-09-08 → 2026-09-17) — plusieurs sections ci-dessus sont maintenant obsolètes

**Vrais volumes (obtenus via `slapcat`, pas `ldapsearch` — le bind anonyme/simple plafonne silencieusement à 500 résultats, même paginé) :** mtq=64 492, guy=121 461, gua=121 455. **Pilote changé : `ool.fr` (12 comptes sur mtq), pas `business.ool.fr`.** `business.ool.fr` a un vrai volume de 270 sur mtq (972 sur guy/gua) et contient des entrées corrompues (double `@`) confirmées. `rife.re` (3 comptes) écarté aussi : 100 % `deliveryMode: forwardonly`, aucune vraie boîte. `ool.fr` : données propres, `userPassword` en `{SHA}` (pas `{SSHA}`), `accountStatus` validé exhaustivement sur les 64 492 comptes mtq (`active` 64491 + `enabled` 1 — `an.jean-louis`, seul outlier).

**Découverte systémique : format legacy `sentmail-*`** — 59 486 fichiers sur tout mtq (webmail 2012-2014, hors structure Maildir++ standard), nécessite un vrai script de conversion avant bascule, pas un correctif ponctuel.

**Décision architecture (confirmée avec l'utilisateur) :** on ne migre PAS l'annuaire LDAP vers Postfix — `slapd` reste sur `smtp-mtq-1`, Dovecot l'interroge à distance via un compte de service dédié (`cn=dovecot-auth,ou=services,o=ool`, en cours de création, `rootdn` = `cn=admin,o=ool` retrouvé dans `/etc/openldap/slapd.conf`). Ça évite deux copies divergentes de la vérité pendant la transition et permet un rollback simple.

**⚠️ Nouveau fait critique (2026-09-17), confirmé par l'utilisateur : `smtp-mtq-1` sera éteint définitivement** une fois qmail décommissionné. Ça veut dire que la décision ci-dessus n'est valable que pendant la transition — **avant l'extinction de `smtp-mtq-1`, il faudra migrer/relocaliser `slapd` et sa base LDAP vers une machine qui va rester en vie**, sinon Dovecot perd sa source d'authentification. C'est une tâche distincte et différée, pas un blocage pour le travail en cours (créer le compte de service `dovecot-auth` reste utile immédiatement). À demander : ce même sort (extinction) s'applique-t-il aussi à `smtp-guy-1`/`smtp-gua-1` ?

**How to apply :** Avant toute proposition de "fin de projet", vérifier explicitement si `slapd`/LDAP a été relocalisé hors de `smtp-mtq-1` (et des autres sites source si applicable) — ne pas supposer que la migration qmail→Postfix suffit pour permettre l'extinction des serveurs sources.

Let's check that against the math, because the numbers still don't quite fit "all three merged."

## The math doesn't support "combined mtq + guy + gua"

- If all three were simply added together (assuming no overlap): 64,492 + 121,461 + 121,455 = **307,408**

That's far short of either estimate — and suspiciously close to *just* guy/gua's size alone (off by the same few-hundred-account drift we already saw between guy and gua themselves). There doesn't seem to be room in that number for mtq's 64,492 accounts to be folded in on top.

Analogy: if someone tells you a box contains three separate collections combined, but the box only weighs as much as one of the three collections alone, the other two probably aren't actually in there.

## 1. The real scope (took real work to establish)

Four LDAP servers matter here, not three:

| Server | Role | Real account count |
|---|---|---|
| `smtp-mtq-1` | Martinique — independent, small | **64,492** |
| `smtp-guy-1` | Guyane | **121,461** |
| `smtp-gua-1` | Guadeloupe | **121,455** |
| `172.30.37.225` ("ldap") | Discovered late — likely the real source for guy/gua | **121,858** |

Every early estimate (1, then 270, then 500) was wrong because plain `ldapsearch` silently caps at 500 results on this directory. `slapcat` (direct disk read, bypasses the LDAP protocol limit entirely) gave the real numbers.

We initially thought `172.30.37.225` fed a "copy" into `smtp-mtq-1` — checked for `syncrepl`, cron jobs, systemd timers, found none, and when we compared domain fingerprints (`ool.fr` = 47,643 there vs. mtq's 12), it became clear `172.30.37.225` is actually guy/gua's lineage, completely unrelated to mtq's dataset. Correctly filed away for later, not blocking current work.

## 2. Pilot domain: `ool.fr` (12 accounts on mtq)

Chosen over `business.ool.fr` (270 accounts, contains double-`@` corrupted `mail` values) and `rife.re` (3 accounts, but all `deliveryMode: forwardonly` — pure forwards, no real mailbox to test with). Verified clean data, `{SHA}`-hashed passwords (Dovecot-compatible, no resets needed), and validated the login-eligibility rule (`accountStatus: active` or `enabled`) against the **full 64,492-account dataset** — caught that one account (`an.jean-louis`) uses `enabled` instead of `active`.

## 3. The `sentmail-*` legacy format (resolved, and it's big)

One account had 19 files in a non-standard "Sent" folder format from a 2012–2014 webmail app. Chasing the real scope was its own debugging saga — a `-maxdepth` mistake, then `find` mysteriously returning nothing because **`/var/qmail/maildirs` is itself a symlink** (fixed with `-L`). Final number: **59,486 files across mtq** — a systemic conversion task, not a one-off fix, needed before migration.

## 4. Auth wiring (Postfix + Dovecot) — where we are now

We just confirmed there are **no other accounts with write access** in this directory at all — no delegated service accounts, nothing scoped just for provisioning. content.text:
Found it, and it's a version-specific syntax quirk we should have caught earlier — we actually saw the answer already, in `auth-passwdfile.conf.ext`, and didn't connect the dots.

## Why this happens

This is Dovecot **2.4.1** (shown right in the error banner) — a newer version than the classic `passdb { driver = ... }` syntax most tutorials/docs still show. Dovecot 2.4 requires a **name** after `passdb`/`userdb` to distinguish blocks (so you can have multiple of the same driver type side by side). Remember `auth-passwdfile.conf.ext` from earlier? It was written exactly this way: `passdb passwd-file { ... }`, `userdb passwd-file { ... }` — the name (`passwd-file`) was never optional, it just wasn't obviously a *requirement* until now.

## Fix

```
cat > /etc/dovecot/conf.d/auth-ldap.conf.ext << 'EOF'

I found relevant information about Dovecot 2.4 passdb LDAP configuration. Here are the key findings:

## ldap_uris Configuration

The ldap_uris setting specifies a space separated list of LDAP URIs to connect to. The URIs are in syntax protocol://host:port.

If multiple LDAP servers are specified, it's decided by the LDAP library how the server connections are handled. Typically the first working server is used, and it's never disconnected from. So there is no load balancing or automatic reconnecting to the "primary" server.

## Passdb LDAP Settings

Important passdb LDAP settings include ldap_auth_dn (the authentication DN), ldap_auth_dn_password (the password for authentication), and ldap_base (the base DN for searches).

For Dovecot 2.4, the passdb configuration uses a newer syntax with field definitions. You can configure fields like user, password, proxy, and proxy_timeout within the passdb ldap block.

Additional relevant settings include:
- You can bind anonymously by leaving ldap_auth_dn commented out (useful with passdb_ldap_bind = yes).
- The passdb_use_worker setting enables asynchronous lookups for passdb queries.

For current Dovecot 2.4 documentation, I recommend checking the official Dovecot CE documentation at https://doc.dovecot.org/2.4/.

Based on the search results, here's information about passdb LDAP configuration in Dovecot 2.4 with ldap_filter and fields:

## Filter Configuration

The passdb_ldap_filter specifies how a user is found from the LDAP and is used to find the DN for the user.

## Fields Example

Here's a practical example from the Dovecot 2.4 documentation:

A passdb ldap configuration can use fields with user and password mappings like: `user = %{ldap:mailRoutingAddress}` and `password = %{ldap:userPassword}`

The filter for finding the user can be set as: `filter = (mailRoutingAddress=%{user})`

## Complete Configuration Example

A Dovecot 2.4 example shows passdb with `passdb_ldap_filter = (&(objectClass=mailUser)(mailDrop=%{user})(!(mailEnabled=FALSE)))` and fields configured with `user = %{ldap:mailDrop}`, along with userdb using similar filters and additional fields like `home`, `uid`, `gid`, and `quota_storage_size`

These configurations show how to map LDAP attributes to Dovecot's passdb fields using the `%{ldap:attributeName}` syntax for retrieving values from LDAP and filter variables like `%{user}` for search parameters.

```
apt-cache search dovecot | grep -i ldap
```

This checks whether a `dovecot-ldap` (or similarly named) package even exists in the available repos — if it does and it's not installed, that's the actual root cause of this entire saga, not a syntax issue at all.

Quick focus — here's exactly where the current blocker stands.

## The issue in one line

We're trying to wire Dovecot on `mtq-mailsrvp-01` (version **2.4.1**) to authenticate against LDAP, but Dovecot 2.4 completely redesigned its LDAP config syntax — the old "point to an external config file" approach we originally wrote (Phase 4) doesn't work anymore, and we can't find the *correct* new syntax that this specific build will actually accept.

## What's already solid (not the problem)

- The LDAP side is done: `dovecot-auth` service account created and verified in the directory, correct bind DN/password, correct host resolution (`smtp-mtq-1.ool.fr`), correct file permissions.
- We know the exact filter logic we need (`accountStatus: active`/`enabled`, excluding `forwardonly`) and the exact attribute mappings (`mail`→user, `userPassword`→password, `mailMessageStore`→home) — none of that content is in question, just how to *express* it in 2.4's syntax.

## Where we're actually stuck

Every variant we've tried for the `passdb ldap { }` / `userdb ldap { }` blocks gets rejected by `doveconf -n` with "Unknown setting":
- `args = <path>` (the old style) — rejected
- `passdb_ldap_args` — rejected
- `passdb_ldap_filter` nested inside the block — rejected
- `passdb_ldap_filter` at top level — rejected
- plain `filter = ...` inside the block — rejected

Official Dovecot docs (`doc.dovecot.org`) are returning `503` on every fetch attempt (likely bot-blocked), and third-party sources are giving inconsistent answers mixing different Dovecot versions (2.3/2.4.1/2.4.4/3.0).

## The real lead we just found

We extracted actual strings from the compiled Dovecot binaries — `passdb_ldap_filter` genuinely exists as a compiled-in identifier, but `doveconf` still won't accept it. And critically: **there's no separate LDAP auth module file anywhere on this box** (`/usr/lib/dovecot/modules/` only has the unrelated Sieve-LDAP plugin), and `dpkg -l` shows no `dovecot-ldap` package installed.

**Working theory**: LDAP passdb/userdb support might need its own separate package on this Debian build, and it's simply not installed — which would make this a packaging gap, not a syntax mistake we haven't found yet.

**Next step, not yet run**: `apt-cache search dovecot | grep -i ldap` — to confirm whether such a package exists and just needs installing.

# Qmail → Postfix/Dovecot Migration — Outremer Telecom

**Status:** In progress (pilot domain phase)
**Last updated:** 2026-09-22

## 1. Project Overview

Outremer Telecom operates mail service across three regional sites — Martinique (`mtq`), Guadeloupe (`gua`), and Guyane (`guy`) — each running a legacy **qmail-ldap** stack with its own local LDAP directory. The goal is to migrate all mail service to a single, unified **Postfix + Dovecot + Roundcube** platform (`mtq-mailsrvp-01`), retiring the legacy qmail servers over time.

**Strategy:** domain-by-domain migration rather than a single cutover, starting with the smallest, cleanest domain as a pilot before tackling larger, riskier domains.

**Architecture decision:** during the transition, the existing LDAP directories are **not** migrated or copied. Dovecot authenticates directly against the existing source LDAP over the network, using a dedicated, read-only service account. This keeps qmail and Postfix reading from a single, unchanged source of truth throughout the migration — avoiding divergent copies of account data and enabling a simple rollback if needed.

## 2. Infrastructure Map

| Server | Role | Real account count | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `smtp-mtq-1` | Martinique qmail-ldap source | 64,492 | Scheduled for full decommission once qmail is retired |
| `smtp-guy-1` | Guyane qmail-ldap source | 121,461 | Near-identical data to `gua` |
| `smtp-gua-1` | Guadeloupe qmail-ldap source | 121,455 | Near-identical data to `guy`; no native LDAP replication found (no `syncrepl`/`contextCSN`) between them — likely application-level dual-write |
| `172.30.37.225` | LDAP server, matches guy/gua's data fingerprint | 121,858 | Likely the true upstream source for guy/gua; confirmed unrelated to mtq's dataset |
| `mtq-mailsrvp-01` | Target Postfix/Dovecot/Roundcube platform | — | Already hosts other live Postfix virtual domains via a separate flat-file auth mechanism |

**Important methodology note:** standard `ldapsearch` queries against these directories silently cap at 500 results (server-side size limit), which produced badly wrong early estimates. Accurate counts require `slapcat` (direct database read, bypasses the LDAP protocol limit).

## 3. Key Data-Quality Findings

- **`mail` attribute corruption:** some entries store a malformed double-`@` address (e.g. `user@domainA@domainB`) — a genuine source data defect, not a search artifact.
- **Legacy webmail Sent-folder format:** a non-standard flat-file format (`sentmail-<pid>.<timestamp>`) from a 2012–2014-era webmail application affects **59,486 files** across `mtq` alone — a systemic issue requiring a dedicated conversion step (not a one-off fix) before these folders are visible in the new IMAP structure.
- **`accountStatus` is not uniform:** across all 64,492 `mtq` accounts, only two values exist — `active` (64,491) and `enabled` (1 account) — both must be treated as valid/eligible for login.
- **Password hashing:** `userPassword` uses the `{SHA}` scheme (unsalted SHA-1) consistently, which Dovecot supports natively — no password resets required for end users.
- **Two Maildir path conventions coexist:** `d1/<first-letter>/<user>` (older) and `d2/<numeric-bucket>/<user>` (newer) — any migration tooling must handle both.
- **`smtp-mtq-1` will be fully powered off** once qmail is decommissioned. LDAP (`slapd`) currently runs on that same box — it will need to be relocated to a surviving host **before** that decommission, as a distinct, separate task.

## 4. Pilot Domain: `ool.fr`

Selected over two other small-domain candidates after closer inspection:
- `rife.re` (3 accounts) — rejected: all accounts are `deliveryMode: forwardonly` (pure mail forwards, no real mailbox to migrate).
- `business.ool.fr` (270 accounts on mtq) — rejected: contains known `mail` attribute corruption.
- **`ool.fr` (12 accounts)** — selected: clean data, real mailboxes, ~80% concentrated on a single physical mail host.

## 5. Current Status by Phase

| Phase | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm auth architecture (Dovecot reads existing LDAP directly) | ✅ Done |
| 2 | Map required LDAP attributes to Dovecot fields | ✅ Done |
| 3 | Create dedicated read-only LDAP bind account (`cn=dovecot-auth,ou=services,o=ool`) | ✅ Done |
| 4 | Define auth filter logic (status whitelist + forward-only exclusion), validated against the full 64,492-account dataset | ✅ Done |
| 5 | Wire LDAP passdb/userdb into Dovecot's auth configuration | 🔶 In progress — blocked on Dovecot 2.4's substantially redesigned LDAP configuration syntax (see below) |
| 6 | Enable Postfix↔Dovecot SASL authentication | ⏳ Not started |
| 7 | Test authentication against the 12 `ool.fr` accounts | ⏳ Not started |
| 8 | Convert legacy Sent-folder data, migrate Maildir content, cutover | ⏳ Not started |

### Current blocker (Phase 5)

`mtq-mailsrvp-01` runs **Dovecot 2.4.1**, which replaced the classic LDAP configuration format (an external config file referenced via `args =`) with a new inline syntax. Multiple setting-name variants have been tested and rejected by `doveconf -n`; official documentation is currently unreachable (503 errors), and third-party sources give inconsistent answers across Dovecot versions. Current working theory: LDAP passdb/userdb support may require a separate package not yet installed on this host (no LDAP auth module found under `/usr/lib/dovecot/modules/`, and no `dovecot-ldap`-style package listed by `dpkg`) — pending verification via `apt-cache search`.

## 6. Open Items / Risks

- **Legacy webmail data**: scope and conversion plan for the 59,486 `sentmail-*` files needs to be finalized before any domain migrates.
- **Stuck mail queue**: `smtp-mtq-1` has ~31,000 messages stuck in its qmail queue — appears unrelated to this migration but has not yet been investigated; may indicate a live delivery problem.
- **Account deduplication**: the true unique total across `mtq` + `guy` + `gua` (+ the newly discovered `172.30.37.225`) is not yet finalized.
- **Contacts/address book location**: not stored in LDAP or Maildir; source system not yet identified.
- **guy vs. gua live traffic**: which of the two actually serves live production traffic (vs. standby) has not been conclusively determined.
- **LDAP relocation**: required before `smtp-mtq-1` is decommissioned (see §3).
- **Admin credential reuse**: the LDAP `rootdn` (`cn=admin`) password is currently identical across at least `smtp-mtq-1` and `172.30.37.225` — worth addressing as a security hardening item post-migration.

## 7. Next Steps

1. Resolve the Dovecot 2.4 LDAP configuration syntax (Phase 5) — currently checking for a missing package dependency.
2. Complete Phase 6 (Postfix SASL) and Phase 7 (test authentication on `ool.fr`).
3. Design and validate the legacy Sent-folder conversion tooling.
4. Investigate the `smtp-mtq-1` mail queue backlog.
5. Plan LDAP relocation ahead of `smtp-mtq-1`'s eventual decommission.

# Migration qmail → Postfix/Dovecot — Outremer Telecom

**Statut :** en cours (phase du domaine pilote)
**Dernière mise à jour :** 2026-09-22

## 1. Vue d'ensemble du projet

Outremer Telecom exploite le service de messagerie sur trois sites régionaux — Martinique (`mtq`), Guadeloupe (`gua`) et Guyane (`guy`) — chacun avec sa propre infrastructure legacy **qmail-ldap** et son annuaire LDAP local. L'objectif est de migrer l'ensemble du service de messagerie vers une plateforme unifiée **Postfix + Dovecot + Roundcube** (`mtq-mailsrvp-01`), avec un décommissionnement progressif des serveurs qmail legacy.

**Stratégie :** migration domaine par domaine plutôt qu'une bascule unique, en commençant par le domaine le plus petit et le plus propre comme pilote avant d'attaquer les domaines plus gros et plus risqués.

**Décision d'architecture :** pendant la transition, les annuaires LDAP existants ne sont **ni migrés ni copiés**. Dovecot s'authentifie directement contre le LDAP source, via le réseau, avec un compte de service dédié en lecture seule. Cela garantit que qmail et Postfix lisent tous les deux la même source de vérité, sans jamais diverger, et permet un retour arrière simple en cas de problème.

## 2. Cartographie de l'infrastructure

| Serveur | Rôle | Nombre réel de comptes | Remarques |
|---|---|---|---|
| `smtp-mtq-1` | Source qmail-ldap Martinique | 64 492 | Sera définitivement éteint une fois qmail décommissionné |
| `smtp-guy-1` | Source qmail-ldap Guyane | 121 461 | Données quasi identiques à `gua` |
| `smtp-gua-1` | Source qmail-ldap Guadeloupe | 121 455 | Données quasi identiques à `guy` ; aucune réplication LDAP native trouvée (pas de `syncrepl`/`contextCSN`) — probablement une double écriture applicative |
| `172.30.37.225` | Serveur LDAP dont la signature correspond à guy/gua | 121 858 | Très probablement la vraie source amont de guy/gua ; confirmé sans lien avec les données de mtq |
| `mtq-mailsrvp-01` | Plateforme cible Postfix/Dovecot/Roundcube | — | Héberge déjà d'autres domaines Postfix en production via un mécanisme d'authentification par fichier plat distinct |

**Remarque méthodologique importante :** les recherches `ldapsearch` classiques sur ces annuaires plafonnent silencieusement à 500 résultats (limite côté serveur), ce qui a produit de très mauvaises estimations initiales. Les comptages fiables nécessitent `slapcat` (lecture directe de la base, sans passer par cette limite du protocole LDAP).

## 3. Principales anomalies de données identifiées

- **Corruption de l'attribut `mail`** : certaines entrées stockent une adresse malformée avec un double `@` (ex. `utilisateur@domaineA@domaineB`) — un vrai défaut de la donnée source, pas un artefact de recherche.
- **Format legacy des e-mails envoyés** : un format à plat non standard (`sentmail-<pid>.<horodatage>`), hérité d'une application webmail utilisée entre 2012 et 2014, concerne **59 486 fichiers** rien que sur `mtq` — un problème systémique nécessitant un vrai script de conversion (pas un correctif ponctuel) avant que ces dossiers soient visibles dans la nouvelle structure IMAP.
- **`accountStatus` non uniforme** : sur les 64 492 comptes `mtq`, seules deux valeurs existent — `active` (64 491) et `enabled` (1 compte) — les deux doivent être traitées comme valides pour la connexion.
- **Hachage des mots de passe** : `userPassword` utilise systématiquement le schéma `{SHA}` (SHA-1 non salé), nativement supporté par Dovecot — aucune réinitialisation de mot de passe n'est nécessaire pour les utilisateurs.
- **Deux conventions de chemin Maildir coexistent** : `d1/<première-lettre>/<utilisateur>` (ancienne) et `d2/<bucket-numérique>/<utilisateur>` (plus récente) — tout outillage de migration doit gérer les deux.
- **`smtp-mtq-1` sera définitivement éteint** une fois qmail décommissionné. LDAP (`slapd`) tourne actuellement sur cette même machine — il faudra le relocaliser vers un hôte pérenne **avant** cette extinction, en tant que tâche distincte.

## 4. Domaine pilote : `ool.fr`

Retenu après analyse détaillée face à deux autres petits domaines candidats :
- `rife.re` (3 comptes) — écarté : tous les comptes sont en `deliveryMode: forwardonly` (simples renvois, aucune vraie boîte à migrer).
- `business.ool.fr` (270 comptes sur mtq) — écarté : contient des corruptions connues de l'attribut `mail`.
- **`ool.fr` (12 comptes)** — retenu : données propres, vraies boîtes mail, ~80 % concentrés sur un seul hôte physique de messagerie.

## 5. État d'avancement par phase

| Phase | Description | Statut |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Valider l'architecture d'authentification (Dovecot lit directement le LDAP existant) | ✅ Fait |
| 2 | Cartographier les attributs LDAP requis vers les champs Dovecot | ✅ Fait |
| 3 | Créer le compte de service LDAP dédié en lecture seule (`cn=dovecot-auth,ou=services,o=ool`) | ✅ Fait |
| 4 | Définir la logique du filtre d'authentification (liste blanche de statuts + exclusion des renvois), validée sur les 64 492 comptes réels | ✅ Fait |
| 5 | Câbler `passdb`/`userdb` LDAP dans la configuration d'authentification de Dovecot | 🔶 En cours — bloqué par la syntaxe de configuration LDAP largement refondue de Dovecot 2.4 (voir ci-dessous) |
| 6 | Activer l'authentification SASL Postfix ↔ Dovecot | ⏳ Non commencé |
| 7 | Tester l'authentification sur les 12 comptes `ool.fr` | ⏳ Non commencé |
| 8 | Convertir les données legacy des e-mails envoyés, migrer les Maildirs, bascule | ⏳ Non commencé |

### Blocage actuel (Phase 5)

`mtq-mailsrvp-01` fait tourner **Dovecot 2.4.1**, qui a remplacé le format classique de configuration LDAP (un fichier de configuration externe référencé via `args =`) par une nouvelle syntaxe intégrée. Plusieurs variantes de noms de paramètres ont été testées et rejetées par `doveconf -n` ; la documentation officielle est actuellement inaccessible (erreurs 503), et les sources tierces donnent des réponses incohérentes selon les versions de Dovecot. Piste actuelle : le support LDAP pour `passdb`/`userdb` pourrait nécessiter un paquet séparé non encore installé sur cet hôte (aucun module d'authentification LDAP trouvé sous `/usr/lib/dovecot/modules/`, et aucun paquet de type `dovecot-ldap` listé par `dpkg`) — à vérifier via `apt-cache search`.

## 6. Points ouverts / risques

- **Données webmail legacy** : le périmètre et le plan de conversion des 59 486 fichiers `sentmail-*` doivent être finalisés avant la migration de tout domaine.
- **File d'attente bloquée** : `smtp-mtq-1` a environ 31 000 messages bloqués dans sa file qmail — semble indépendant de cette migration mais n'a pas encore été investigué ; pourrait indiquer un problème de livraison en cours.
- **Dédoublonnage des comptes** : le vrai total unique sur `mtq` + `guy` + `gua` (+ le `172.30.37.225` nouvellement découvert) n'est pas encore finalisé.
- **Localisation des contacts/carnet d'adresses** : ni dans LDAP ni dans les Maildirs ; système source non encore identifié.
- **Trafic réel guy vs gua** : lequel des deux sert réellement le trafic de production (vs. secours) n'a pas été déterminé de façon concluante.
- **Relocalisation de LDAP** : nécessaire avant le décommissionnement de `smtp-mtq-1` (voir §3).
- **Réutilisation d'identifiants admin** : le mot de passe `rootdn` LDAP (`cn=admin`) est actuellement identique au moins entre `smtp-mtq-1` et `172.30.37.225` — à corriger en durcissement de sécurité après la migration.

## 7. Prochaines étapes

1. Résoudre la syntaxe de configuration LDAP de Dovecot 2.4 (Phase 5) — vérification en cours d'une éventuelle dépendance manquante.
2. Terminer la Phase 6 (SASL Postfix) et la Phase 7 (test d'authentification sur `ool.fr`).
3. Concevoir et valider l'outillage de conversion des e-mails envoyés legacy.
4. Enquêter sur la file d'attente bloquée de `smtp-mtq-1`.
5. Planifier la relocalisation de LDAP avant le décommissionnement de `smtp-mtq-1`.

content.text:
It's everybody's favorite time, KOBY BOWSER TIME!

Here's the full state of play on the qmail → Postfix migration.

## The setup

Three legacy qmail-ldap sites (`smtp-mtq-1` = 64,492 accounts, `smtp-guy-1` = 121,461, `smtp-gua-1` = 121,455) migrating to a unified Postfix/Dovecot target (`mtq-mailsrvp-01`). Also found a 4th LDAP server (`172.30.37.225`, 121,858 accounts) that turned out to be guy/gua's likely real upstream source — unrelated to mtq. Strategy: domain-by-domain, pilot first.

**Architecture decision:** LDAP stays where it is during the transition — Dovecot queries it remotely via a dedicated read-only service account, rather than migrating/copying the directory. Keeps qmail and Postfix reading the same source of truth, safe rollback if needed.

## Pilot domain: `ool.fr` (12 accounts, mtq)

Chosen over `business.ool.fr` (data corruption) and `rife.re` (pure forwards, no real mailboxes). Clean data, `{SHA}`-hashed passwords (no resets needed), login rule validated against the full 64,492-account dataset (`active` or `enabled` status, excluding `forwardonly`).

## Done

- **Phase 3**: `cn=dovecot-auth,ou=services,o=ool` service account created and verified in LDAP on `smtp-mtq-1`.
- **Phase 4**: auth filter logic and attribute mappings finalized, config file corrected onto the right host (`mtq-mailsrvp-01`) with correct permissions and hostname resolution.
- Identified and quantified a systemic legacy issue: **59,486 "sentmail-\*" files** across mtq from a 2012–2014 webmail app, needing a real conversion tool before migration.
- Wrote a full French project write-up, ready for you to paste into Outline (I can't reach `wiki.corp.intranet.local` myself — internal-only host, no route from my sandbox).

## Currently blocked — Phase 5

Wiring LDAP into Dovecot's auth stack is stuck on **Dovecot 2.4.1's completely redesigned LDAP config syntax**. We've tried multiple setting-name variants (`args`, `passdb_ldap_args`, `passdb_ldap_filter` nested and top-level, plain `filter=`) — all rejected by `doveconf -n`. Official docs are returning 503s, third-party sources are inconsistent across versions. Current lead, not yet checked: **no LDAP auth module exists on the box, and no `dovecot-ldap`-style package shows in `dpkg -l`** — working theory is a missing package, not a syntax mistake. Next command queued: `apt-cache search dovecot | grep -i ldap`.

## Still open

- `smtp-mtq-1`'s 31,334-message stuck mail queue (uninvestigated).
- Account dedup across all 4 LDAP sources.
- Where contacts/address books actually live.
- guy vs. gua live-traffic determination.
- LDAP relocation plan before `smtp-mtq-1`'s eventual full shutdown.

Want to run that `apt-cache search` now and get Phase 5 unstuck?

Carefully consider the reversibility and blast radius of actions. Generally you can freely take local, reversible actions like editing files or running tests. But for actions that are hard to reverse, affect shared systems beyond your local environment, or could otherwise be risky or destructive, check with the user before proceeding. The cost of pausing to confirm is low, while the cost of an unwanted action (lost work, unintended messages sent, deleted branches) can be very high. For actions like these, consider the context, the action, and user instructions, and by default transparently communicate the action and ask for confirmation before proceeding. This default can be changed by user instructions - if explicitly asked to operate more autonomously, then you may proceed without confirmation, but still attend to the risks and consequences when taking actions. A user approving an action (like a git push) once does NOT mean that they approve it in all contexts, so unless actions are authorized in advance in durable instructions like CLAUDE.md files, always confirm first. ```markdown
---
name: {{short-kebab-case-slug}}
description: {{one-line summary, used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}
metadata:
  type: {{user, feedback, project, reference}}
---

{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].}}
```

A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

- If the memory names a file path: check the file exists.
- If the memory names a function or flag: grep for it.
- If the user is about to act on your recommendation (not just asking about history), verify first.

The distinction is often that memory can be recalled in future conversations and should not be used for persisting information that is only useful within the scope of the current conversation.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.


## Writing the prompt

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>

  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"

User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>

A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.

Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
